caption: WER during fine-tuning Whisper model with different amount of weights
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the Word Error Rate (WER) during the fine-tuning of a Whisper model of type "tiny" across six epochs, comparing different quantization and adaptation strategies. The x-axis represents the epoch, ranging from 0 to 6 with a linear scale and integer tick labels at each epoch. The y-axis represents WER, ranging from 20 to 70 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 10. Five distinct lines are shown, each corresponding to a different fine-tuning configuration: "tiny AdaLoRA_int4" (gray solid line with circular markers), "tiny AdaLoRA_int8" (gray dashed line with square markers), "tiny int4" (gray dash-dotted line with circular markers), "tiny int8" (gray dash-dotted line with square markers), and "tiny full" (gray dotted line with triangular markers). At epoch 0, the WER values are approximately 70 for "tiny AdaLoRA_int4", 60 for "tiny AdaLoRA_int8", 60 for "tiny int4", 55 for "tiny int8", and 30 for "tiny full". All lines show a general downward trend as epoch increases, indicating decreasing WER with training progress. The "tiny full" configuration consistently achieves the lowest WER, starting at 30 and decreasing to about 25 by epoch 6. The "tiny AdaLoRA_int4" line starts highest at 70 and decreases to around 35 by epoch 6. The "tiny int4" line decreases from 60 to approximately 40, while "tiny int8" decreases from 55 to about 38. The "tiny AdaLoRA_int8" line decreases from 60 to roughly 33. All lines exhibit a steeper decline in the early epochs, with the rate of improvement slowing down after epoch 3.
